title: Croque Madame
subtitle: French toasted ham and cheese sandwich with a fried egg
excerpt: The croque-monsieur with a fried egg on top: white bread spread with béchamel, layered with cooked ham and Gruyère, grilled until the cheese bubbles, then topped with a fried egg. Excellent for lunch or a late breakfast with a glass of white wine.

recipe.sourceNotes: The croque-madame is the croque-monsieur (which has appeared on Parisian café menus since at least 1910) with the addition of a fried egg on top. The name is a reference to the hat-like appearance of the egg, supposedly resembling the hats worn by ladies (madame) of the era. The key difference between a croque-monsieur and a straightforward toasted cheese sandwich is the béchamel: spread inside the sandwich and on top before grilling, it provides richness and prevents the bread from drying out. The combination of béchamel, ham, Gruyère, and the runny yolk from the egg creates a sauce within the dish when you cut into it.

content.text: Make the béchamel just thick enough to spread without running off the bread. Spread it inside and on top of the sandwich before grilling; the top layer will bubble and colour under the grill. The grill must be very hot so the cheese colours before the bread becomes dry. Fry the egg at the last moment so the yolk is still runny when the sandwich comes out.

items.preparation: cooked ham; 2 to 3 thin slices per sandwich

content.text: Make a béchamel: melt the butter, add the flour and stir for 1 minute. Gradually add the milk, whisking constantly, until thick and smooth, about 4 minutes. Season with salt, nutmeg, and mustard. Remove from the heat.

Toast the bread lightly. Spread béchamel on all 4 slices. Layer ham and half the Gruyère on 2 slices. Top with the remaining bread, béchamel-side in. Spread more béchamel on top and scatter with the remaining Gruyère. Place under a very hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden.
While the sandwiches grill, fry the eggs in a little oil until the whites are set and the yolks remain runny. Slide a fried egg onto each sandwich immediately before serving.
